title: The One O’Clock Piper
description:
Add a touch of Highland tradition to your visit with our One O’clock Piper, performing live from the castle's Flag Tower above the Great Glen View Roof Terrace - every Thursday, Saturday and Sunday.

Included with your Experience ticket, this special performance lets lunchtime visitors enjoy the unmistakable sound of the bagpipes in a spectacular setting, overlooking Inverness and the Highlands.

After the performance, you can meet the piper and take a quick photo, creating a memorable keepsake from your visit. Or, if you're exploring the Castle Gardens, simply pause and enjoy the music as it carries across the heart of the city.

Experience this warm Highland welcome as part of your visit.
address: The Inverness Castle Experience, Castle St, Castle Hill, Inverness, IV2 3EG
venue_name: The Inverness Castle Experience

title: Spirit Cèilidh
description:
As November draws to a close and Scotland gets ready to celebrate St Andrew's Day, join us for a lively evening of music, dancing, good food and great company at The Inverness Castle Experience.

Start the evening with a hearty serving of traditional stovies before the music begins and the dance floor comes to life. With live Scottish music and friendly cèilidh callers on hand to guide you through every dance, it's easy to join in, whether you've been to a hundred cèilidhs or it's your very first one.

Bring your friends, gather your family or come along and meet new people. Expect plenty of laughter, lots of dancing and a warm Highland welcome throughout the evening.

What to Expect

  • A hearty serving of traditional Scottish stovies

  • Live Scottish music

  • Friendly cèilidh callers to guide every dance

  • No experience needed, join in and have fun

  • A relaxed, social atmosphere

  • The chance to celebrate with friends old and new

Good to Know

  • No previous cèilidh experience is required

  • You don't need to bring a partner

  • The dances are explained as you go

  • Come as you are. There's no dress code

The ticket includes stovies and cèilidh entertainment.
address: Saltire Bistro, The Inverness Castle Experience, Castle St, Castle Hill, Inverness, IV2 3EG

title: Breakfast with Santa
description:
Create a new festive tradition in the heart of the Highlands as Santa, or Bodach na Nollaig as he's known in Gaelic, makes a very special stop at The Inverness Castle Experience.

Before taking their seats, little ones will be welcomed by one of Santa's helpers in the Saltire Bistro for a delicious festive breakfast. Then, the moment everyone has been waiting for... Santa will visit each family's table, creating a special Christmas memory.

The festive fun continues with a Christmas craft for every child, the chance to choose their own special gift from Santa's workshop in the Castle Shop, and the opportunity to send their Christmas wish on its way at the castle's very own wishing well.

With festive treats, magical moments, and a special visit from the man himself, Breakfast with Santa at The Inverness Castle Experience is a wonderful way to make treasured memories together. As families share breakfast and festive cheer, they'll create moments that become part of their own Christmas story.

The festive fun continues with a Christmas craft for every child, the chance to choose their own special gift from Santa's workshop in the Castle Shop, and the opportunity to send their Christmas wish on its way at the castle's very own wishing well.

title: Spirit Tasting with Guests: The Cairn
description:

WHISKY PRESENT — Benromach

An immersive Christmas whisky experience that brings the story of The Cairn to life through its past, present and future.

Three whiskies. Three chapters. One remarkable story.

title: Stories from Castle Hill: William Fraser Tytler
description:
Join Highland Archive Service Community Engagement Officer Lorna Steele-McGinn for an illustrated history talk exploring the life of William Fraser Tytler and the events, both everyday and extraordinary, that helped shape the story and image of Inverness and the wider Highlands.

Writer, historian, lecturer, lawyer and sheriff, William Fraser Tytler led a remarkable and complex life. His travels took him across the Highlands, where he intervened in famine-stricken communities and played a significant role in the development of the region. He inherited enslaved people on a Jamaican plantation and later instigated the construction of the present-day Inverness Castle in the 1830s and 1840s, helping to create one of the city's most recognisable landmarks and leaving a legacy that continues to shape Inverness today.

Tea, coffee and a scone are included.

title: Weaving Burns: A Tartan in Verse
description:
Join acclaimed Highland weaver and Prickly Thistle founder Clare Campbell for a relaxed, creative workshop celebrating the life and Spirit of Robert Burns.

Set in the atmospheric North Tower Bar in the Cèilidh Rooms at The Inverness Castle Experience, this small-group session offers a rare chance to learn from one of the Highlands' most celebrated makers.

Inspired by a favourite Burns poem, you'll explore how words, stories and emotions are translated into colour and pattern before creating your own tartan design. Using a traditional card loom, Clare will guide you through the weaving process, helping you create a small tartan swatch to take home.

Whether you're a lover of Scottish culture, creativity or simply keen to try something new, this is a unique chance to spend time with a local maker whose work is putting Highland textiles on the world stage.

Your ticket includes:

  • A small-group weaving workshop with Clare Campbell of Prickly Thistle

  • A glass of prosecco and nibbles on arrival

  • All materials and use of a traditional card loom

  • Guidance in creating a tartan inspired by a Burns poem

  • Your own handwoven tartan swatch to take home

  • Time to learn about tartan, storytelling and Highland craftsmanship

  • A unique experience in the North Tower Bar at The Inverness Castle Experience

Leave with a one-of-a-kind keepsake and a new appreciation for the threads that connect Scotland's stories, culture and creativity.

description:

title: Stories from Castle Hill: The Highlands at War
description:
From the Lovat Scouts to the Special Military Area: The Highlands at war. Join Highland Archive Service Community Engagement Officer Lorna Steele-McGinn for a series of illustrated history talks focusing on both the everyday and the seismic events which have shaped the story and the image of Inverness and the wider Highlands.

It was the skills and experience of Highland gamekeepers that led to the creation of the Lovat Scouts during the Boer War. It was the specific terrain of Lochaber that made the area perfect for training commandos during WWII. No wonder a large swathe of the Highlands was repeatedly designated a special military area…
